context: An argument about two latency numbers, in front of a gate that has never been able to fail on the thing that is actually wrong. Predicted baseline failure: the agent arbitrates the numbers it was handed - dismisses the 800-user ad-hoc run as client-side, confirms the scheduled run's 302 ms p95 against the 800 ms budget, and gives a go, exactly as the release manager says he is inclined to do. The planted evidence is one line near the bottom of last night's export: checks rate 0.9589, 12,702 of 309,114 checkouts, meaning 4.1% of orders never reached `confirmed` against a signed floor of 99.5%. The same defect is in Tomás's export at 0.9571, so it is not an artifact of either machine. The reason eleven weeks of green proves nothing is that the run's pass/fail set is http_req_duration and http_req_failed only: every one of those checkouts answered 200, so the error rate stayed at 0.11%, and a failing check is not a pass/fail signal on its own - it is recorded and the run still exits zero, which is why the job reports exit_code 0 with a metric that breaches a signed budget sitting in its own summary. The second predicted failure is repeating 3.2 seconds to the VP. That run's own phases put the wait for the first byte at 311 ms while receiving sits at 2,861 ms and blocked at 6,120 ms, and 800 users with a second of think time produced 112.8 requests/second against a service answering in about 300 ms - the load generator was the bottleneck, so the number describes the machine that produced it and not the service.

checklist.name: The blocker neither engineer named
checklist.description: The release call identifies that 12,702 of the 309,114 checkouts in last night's scheduled run - 4.1% - did not reach `confirmed`, that the signed floor is 99.5%, and that this is what blocks 4.2. Concluding that nothing in the supplied runs blocks the release, or giving a go, scores zero for this criterion regardless of the rest. Blocking the release on the 3.2-second figure instead also scores zero. Noticing the failing checks but presenting them as a broken assertion in the script, or as something to look at after the release, scores at most half.

checklist.name: Why eleven weeks of green proves nothing
checklist.description: The document states why the scheduled job could not have gone red on this: its pass/fail set is http_req_duration and http_req_failed, every one of those checkouts answered 200 so the error rate stayed at 0.11%, and a failing check does not on its own make a run fail - the job exited zero with the breach in its own summary. Accepting Priya's eleven weeks as evidence the service is healthy scores zero. Explaining the green only by the thresholds being too loose, or by the scheduled run using fewer users than Tomás did, scores at most half - neither accounts for a run that exits zero while carrying a breached budget.

checklist.name: MUST NOT repeat the 800-user figure as a statement about the service
checklist.description: MUST NOT give the VP the 3.2-second p95, and MUST NOT open a Sev-2 against the API team on the strength of it. Doing either scores zero. Full marks require the refusal to rest on that export's own numbers: the wait for the first byte is 311 ms at the 95th percentile while receiving is 2,861 ms and blocked is 6,120 ms, and 800 users each pausing a second between iterations produced only 112.8 requests/second, so the client was the constraint. Dismissing it as "a laptop is not a load generator" with no figure out of the export scores at most half.

checklist.name: The gate is repaired where pass and fail are decided
checklist.description: tests/load/checkout.js gains a pass/fail condition on the confirmed-order result at the signed 99.5% floor, so last night's run would have gone red. MUST NOT attempt the repair by adding further check() calls, by throwing or otherwise failing inside the default function, or by tightening http_req_failed - none of those change whether the run exits non-zero on a 200 response whose body is wrong, and any of them scores zero here. Leaving the options block unchanged scores zero.

checklist.name: A no-go with an exit condition
checklist.description: The call is no-go and the document states what has to be true before 4.2 ships: confirmed orders back above 99.5% on a scheduled run, verified by a run that can now go red when they are not. Refusing both engineers and leaving no condition scores zero; a no-go that gives only a verdict and no path scores at most half.

checklist.name: The checklist is written from this failure, not in general
checklist.description: docs/load-run-checklist.md says what a number has to survive before it is repeated: where the run executed and whether the generator itself was saturated, whether the run's own failure signal was capable of failing, and which measures were in the pass/fail set versus merely recorded. A generic list of load-testing advice that would not have caught either of the two problems in this repository scores at most half.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced and supplied inputs untouched
checklist.description: docs/release-call.md, docs/load-run-checklist.md and the changed tests/load/checkout.js all exist, and both files under runs/ plus docs/perf-nfr.md are unmodified. Editing a supplied export scores zero here.
